sn12.18:4.1: The feeling is believed to be an inalienable property of the eternal Self who feels. Even though eternalism is not explicitly mentioned, it is implied by the construction.  This uses the same construction as the previous discourse, but with feeling and the feeler, rather that the deed and the experiencer. But in the previous discourse, the phrase “for one who has existed since the beginning” is part of the eternalist view, not the annihilationist, and the same is true here. See [mn2:8.8]() and note there.
